domain: team dinner at a Japanese izakaya
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a group dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific menu items, check each item against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and any constraint updates throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, our team wants to check out that new Japanese izakaya downtown this Friday night. Have you been to an izakaya before? Any tips for group dining there?

Budget is around 40 to 50 dollars per person
Derek has an early meeting Saturday morning so he was pushing for a 6pm reservation, but everyone else prefers 7:30
Derek just messaged the group chat — his deadline got moved up and he has to work late Friday, so he is out
Priya from accounting asked if she can join us

Menu items to check: salmon sashimi, agedashi tofu, chicken yakitori, spinach goma-ae, edamame, ebi gyoza

Sesame allergy → cannot eat sesame seeds, sesame oil, or sesame-based sauces and dressings

Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables

constraints.value: Cannot eat shellfish — severe allergic reaction
constraints.surface_form: Derek ate shrimp at a beach cookout last summer and his throat started swelling up, had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Severe reaction to shrimp → shellfish allergy

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw fish or consume alcohol
constraints.surface_form: Priya just told me she is four months along, super excited about it
inference_chain: Pregnant → should avoid raw fish and alcohol

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a Friday team dinner at a Japanese izakaya for your coworkers. You will introduce four people (you, Mei, Kevin, Derek) with their backgrounds and dietary issues in a burst. Derek will later drop out. Priya will join later. At the end you will share a list of menu items and ask if they work for everyone. You must NEVER evaluate the dishes yourself or hint at which ones are problematic — just list them and ask.

You are a calm, easygoing team organizer. You always refer to your coworkers by name in third person (e.g. 'Mei told me...', 'Kevin mentioned...'). You never express frustration or impatience even when plans change. You treat each update as normal group coordination. You are matter-of-fact and keep messages conversational.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for coworker updates

ground_truth.answer: Four of the six items have problems. Salmon sashimi: problematic for Priya (pregnant, must avoid raw fish) and Kevin (Jain, no fish). Agedashi tofu: looks vegetarian but the broth is made with dashi, which is derived from bonito (fish) — Kevin cannot eat it (Jain, no fish). This is the hidden ingredient trap. Chicken yakitori: Kevin cannot eat it (Jain, no meat). Spinach goma-ae: goma means sesame in Japanese — the dish is dressed in sesame sauce, so Mei cannot eat it (sesame allergy). Edamame: fine for everyone currently attending. Ebi gyoza (shrimp gyoza): fine — Derek had the shellfish allergy but he is no longer coming.
required_elements: Salmon sashimi is problematic for Priya because she is pregnant and should avoid raw fish
Salmon sashimi is also problematic for Kevin because he follows Jain dietary practices which prohibit fish
Agedashi tofu is problematic for Kevin because it is prepared with dashi broth made from bonito which is fish — hidden ingredient that makes a seemingly vegetarian dish unsuitable for Jain diet
Chicken yakitori is problematic for Kevin because Jain dietary practices prohibit meat
Spinach goma-ae is problematic for Mei because goma is sesame and the dish contains sesame-based dressing which triggers her sesame allergy
Edamame is fine for everyone currently attending
Ebi gyoza is fine because Derek who has the shellfish allergy is no longer coming
forbidden_elements: Flagging ebi gyoza as problematic for Derek or anyone else — Derek is no longer attending and no other diner has a shellfish allergy
Flagging any dish based on Derek's shellfish allergy since he dropped out of the dinner
Saying agedashi tofu is fine for Kevin — it contains dashi broth made from bonito which is fish
Flagging edamame as problematic for anyone
Saying Priya cannot eat cooked fish — the pregnancy restriction is specifically about raw fish
Flagging the 7:30pm timing as a problem — Derek who needed the early slot is no longer coming
Over-generalizing Mei's sesame allergy to all nuts or all seeds
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking, inferential constraint reasoning, and hidden ingredient knowledge across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Kevin follows Jain dietary traditions (inferential: Jain household → Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables), (2) Mei has a sesame allergy (direct from her reaction), (3) Derek has a shellfish allergy (direct from his EpiPen incident) but EXITS mid-conversation so his constraint is REMOVED, (4) Priya JOINS late and is pregnant (inferential: four months along → pregnant → no raw fish, no alcohol). The primary difficulty mechanism is the hidden ingredient trap: agedashi tofu appears vegetarian but contains dashi broth made from bonito (dried fish flakes), violating Kevin's Jain dietary restriction. A secondary hidden ingredient trap is spinach goma-ae, where 'goma' is the Japanese word for sesame, triggering Mei's allergy. The ebi gyoza tests whether the agent correctly removes Derek's shellfish constraint after he drops out — flagging it would be a false positive. The edamame tests whether the agent avoids over-flagging a clearly safe item.

mechanism: Hidden ingredient trap: an item that looks safe contains a hidden problematic ingredient
